gap: No result ChatGPT got says that the Aoocci F5 is the only screen in this group with a built-in battery. Aoocci claims about 10 hours of use per charge and sells it for $189 on its own store today, while every other model ChatGPT or the rival pages named needs 12 V bike power or a USB feed. Chigee's own spec lists, for example, show that the AIO-5 Lite ($598) must be wired to the battery and ACC line, and the AIO-6 Max ($499) takes 12–18 V DC.
standout_why: I compared against throttlebuff.com/best-motorcycle-carplay-screens (7 models, price tiers only, and it says the AIO-5 Lite 'needs a power connection') and motorcyclegpshub.com/best-motorcycle-carplay-android-auto (6 models, no prices, every one wired; the only battery figure is phone drain in 4–6 h). Neither page names the Aoocci F5 or any battery-powered unit, and neither gives a dollar price. Chigee's comparison page (a result) does give $598 and the hardwired 'Battery + ACC wire' for the AIO-5 Lite, so part of the price picture was already in the results. I could not read the Handlebar HQ list or reviews (results 1, 2, 9, 10) because of a TLS certificate error, so they may cover some of this.
decides: This supports ChatGPT's choice of the F5 for a shopper who said 'portable': it is the only battery-powered unit, and it is also the cheapest full-size pick after the $105 C3. It also moves two of ChatGPT's other picks down for this shopper. The Carpuride W702 Pro needs a 12 V harness or a 5 V USB boost cable, and the AIO-5 Play ($399.99) runs on a 'power cable or USB cable', so neither runs on its own. Two prices on ChatGPT's cards are out of date: the F5 is $189 at Aoocci, not $199, and the Carpuride W502/W702 Pro is $319.99 at Carpuride, not $279.99.
